title: Software Development Agents: What Works and What Doesn't - Robert Brennan, OpenHands
talk_summary: Robert Brennan of OpenHands describes coding agents as an LLM-in-a-loop with editor/terminal/browser tools, and gives practical guidance on task sizing, prompt specificity, sandboxing, and human review. The most transferable lessons are about task decomposition, prompt specificity to cut token cost, and accountability for agent-authored PRs.

takeaways.technique: Specify the how, not just the what
takeaways.what_they_do: Tell the agent which frameworks, files, and function names to touch, and the strategy (e.g. TDD), so it explores less and produces more accurate output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to tell it not just what you want, but you need to tell it how you want it to do it

takeaways.what_they_do: Scope tasks to one commit with a clear definition of done the agent can self-verify (tests pass, conflicts resolved), and grow task size only as intuition builds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best tasks are things that can be completed pretty quickly. You know, a single commit uh where there's a clear definition of done

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent-opened PRs are attributed to the human who triggered them, so a second human must review and someone owns breakage; anonymous bot PRs were bypassing review and languishing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you open up a poll request with open hands, your face is on that poll request. You're responsible for getting it merged

takeaways.technique: Throw away bad runs instead of iterating
takeaways.what_they_do: If the agent is close, keep iterating in the same conversation to reuse context; if it's way off, discard and restart with a fresh prompt informed by the failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If it's way off though, just throw away that work. Start fresh with a new prompt based on uh what you learned from the last one

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents run in Docker containers isolated from the host, and third-party tokens (GitHub, AWS) are tightly scoped to least privilege.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of our agents run inside of a Docker container by default... make sure that those credentials are tightly scoped

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of raw HTML, pass accessibility trees or markdown to the LLM, and use labeled screenshots for interaction, to avoid wasting tokens on markup cruft.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've had a lot of luck passing it uh accessibility trees or converting to markdown and passing that to the LLM
